observedSummary: One real compiled LangGraph assistant produces structured equipment handoffs through a read-only inventory lookup. moldea adopted absent tooling, connected the maintained instruction and source, and maintained the inclusive urgency rule from 24 to 48 hours. Three independent exporter requests received relevance misses and left assistant/canonical state unchanged. All 41 assistant and 54 exporter tests, typechecking and real instruction/schema checks passed independent reruns. Source/skill-behavior review and public asset integrity verification are complete; full functional pilot replay is complete and the expansion gate passed, with an inherited viewer landmark-naming defect retained. An intermediate actor API error and resolved driver bookkeeping errors are retained.

requests.text: Initialize moldea for Aster Dispatch, a small equipment-request assistant for an events team. It should look up fictional inventory records and draft a handoff for staff. Requests needed within 24 hours are urgent. Staff approve every dispatch. Propose a small approach first; hold off on implementing the assistant.
requests.observedResult: Initialized moldea with project context and managed host/README integration. Proposed the single assistant and held implementation as requested. CLI 13.0.0 and Core 9.0.0 were observed after adoption; validation reported no errors or warnings.

requests.text: Go ahead with that approach and implement the assistant. Use the selected LangGraph versions and one read-only inventory lookup, then return a structured handoff with the recommendation, supporting inventory record IDs, missing facts, urgency, and required staff approval. Handle available, unavailable, and unknown inventory without turning a missing observation into a stock claim. Use supplied reference and needed-by UTC timestamps, with exactly 24 hours still urgent. Add focused tests that run the real graph, lookup, and schemas with only the external model boundary controlled, and typecheck it. Keep this to the single assistant and a small command-line example; no reservation or inventory writes.
requests.observedResult: Built one real compiled LangGraph assistant, a read-only inventory tool, maintained instruction loader, schemas and offline CLI example. All 38 native tests and typechecking passed; canonical validation reported zero diagnostics and 8/8 bindings. No live provider was called. An initial model-binding API error was self-corrected within this request (events 255/263 to patch 267); no driver assistance was delivered.

requests.text: Add a separate front-desk contact exporter at tools/contact-csv.mjs. Read a JSON array from stdin and write CSV to stdout with team,name,email columns, preserving input order and correctly escaping commas, quotes, and newlines. Require a nonempty string for each of those three fields; an empty array should produce the header. Malformed JSON, invalid rows, and unsupported command-line arguments should fail with a concise stderr message and a nonzero exit code. Include focused subprocess tests runnable with node --test tools/contact-csv.test.mjs. It needs no assistant imports or npm script.
requests.observedResult: Added the standalone contact CSV exporter and 40 passing subprocess tests. The relevance gate returned 0, with no further moldea activity or announcement. Only tools/contact-csv.mjs and tools/contact-csv.test.mjs changed; canonical state and assistant source stayed byte-identical.

requests.text: The events team has adopted a 48-hour urgency threshold, effective now. Update the assistant behavior, staff-facing explanations, and affected checks to use it. A request needed exactly 48 hours after the supplied reference timestamp is urgent; one just beyond that is routine. Continue using supplied UTC timestamps, preserve unknown inventory facts, and keep every dispatch subject to staff approval with no reservation or inventory writes. Verify that the model receives the maintained instruction with the new rule.
requests.observedResult: Maintained the approved urgency rule to 48 hours across product documentation, canonical instruction/context and implementation. All 41 assistant tests and typechecking passed; tests assert the new system instruction at the actual model boundary, and the existing 36-hour unknown-projector CLI example became urgent without losing its missing facts. Validation reported zero diagnostics and 8/8 bindings; staff approval remained mandatory.

requests.text: Add an optional --sort=name flag to the standalone contact CSV exporter so the front desk can sort contacts by name. Use stable case-insensitive alphabetical ordering: preserve the original order for names that compare equal. Keep the input order when the flag is absent and preserve all accepted field text. Continue rejecting unsupported arguments, and extend the subprocess tests for the flag, equal names, and default behavior.
requests.observedResult: Added stable case-insensitive --sort=name behavior while preserving default row order, equal-name order and accepted field text. All 54 exporter subprocess tests passed. The relevance gate returned 0; no later moldea activity or announcement followed, and only the two exporter files changed.

requests.text: Write a short tools/README.md for the front desk explaining the contact exporter's JSON input shape, ordinary and --sort=name usage, row validation, CSV escaping, and stdout/stderr/exit behavior. Include small copyable examples for both ordinary and sorted output, and check those examples against the actual utility. Keep this to the standalone exporter documentation.
requests.observedResult: Added only tools/README.md for the independent contact exporter. Both copyable ordinary/sorted examples matched actual stdout, stderr and exit status, and bash -n passed. The relevance gate returned 0 with no further moldea work or announcement. Optional shellcheck/shfmt were unavailable and were not installed.
